finding.claim: PUT /me performs unfiltered mass assignment: Object.assign(req.user, req.body) copies every key of the request body onto the user record, which is then persisted via req.store.save. Any privileged or identity field in the user model (e.g. role, isAdmin, tenantId, id, email, password hash) can be set by an authenticated user. A body with a "__proto__" key also changes req.user's prototype, so inherited property checks could be attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: Object.assign(req.user, req.body) at users.js:5, followed by req.store.save(req.user) at users.js:6 and res.json(req.user) at users.js:7

trace.note: Route PUT /me registered; handler receives req.body (attacker-controlled JSON)
Object.assign copies all own enumerable body keys onto req.user with no allowlist
Mutated req.user persisted unchanged via req.store.save
Sibling handler PUT /me/profile destructures only displayName and bio, showing the intended allowlist was not applied to /me

finding.guards_checked: No validation, sanitizer, allowlist, or schema check on the path in this repo. Ownership is not a concern because req.user is the caller's own record. Auth middleware, user model/schema, and req.store implementation are not in the repo, so whether a dangerous field exists and whether the route is authenticated are UNCERTAIN; impact depends on those.

verdict.guard_found: none. No allowlist, schema, or validation exists on the PUT /me path (users.js:4-7). The sibling /me/profile handler (users.js:11-12) does allowlist displayName and bio, but that does not guard /me.
verdict.reason: The code matches the trace: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no filtering, then users.js:6 saves it and users.js:7 returns it. Whether this is exploitable depends on code outside the repo: the auth middleware that sets req.user, the user model (whether it has role, isAdmin, tenantId, or similar fields), and req.store. The repo does not show any of these, so the privilege-escalation impact cannot be confirmed. The __proto__ claim is also narrower than stated: it only changes the prototype of this one req.user object, not global prototypes.
